definition: A day is FREE only when the snapshot contains no block of any class for it. A day with a published game, an officially anchored all-day event of unknown start time, or only the released-season model does not count as free. This is stricter than asking whether some minutes are free.

classes.PUBLISHED_OFFICIAL: At least one published official game row (official start + estimated duration, official network window, or official date with TBD start).
classes.UNVERIFIED_ANCHOR: No published time, but an officially anchored event occupies the whole day (e.g. Super Bowl, CFP championship, dated college game).
classes.MODEL_ONLY: Only the clearly-labelled 364-day model of unreleased seasons. Still treated as a candidate block.
classes.NO_BLOCK: No block at all in the snapshot.

strict_conclusion: No 7-, 14- or 21-day stretch of consecutive days inside 2027-2029 is free under the strict reading. The longest runs with no published game are short early-winter gaps (see shortlist); every longer empty stretch is empty only because the 2027 NFL/WWO, 2028 and 2029 schedules have not been released, so it cannot be called free.
practical_reading: If 'free' is relaxed to 'not known to contain a game', the longest stretches are the annual late-December/January gap after the college national championship until the next published spring-training or NFL date, and the day ranges that sit between two officially dated events. Those are published explicitly on this page as CANDIDATES, never as verified free time.
